A1.justification: Both complete, readable 18-page PDFs describe AtomicVLA and include Supplementary Material A.1–A.5. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original LIBERO, CALVIN and real-robot experiments, including continual learning and ablations. Appendix A.4 provides additional empirical results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.4 retain the original simulation, real-robot, continual-learning and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical planning/execution procedures, SG-MoE architecture, skill routing, expert expansion and data-generation methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four LIBERO suites, CALVIN ABC-D tasks and real-robot scenarios, including the appendix's complex scenes with irregular objects.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments. CoT-VLA remains in Table 1; its revised average does not represent a changed comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.3 retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The routing ablations in Table 5, appendix task-level failure analysis, expert-count/latency comparison and error-recovery demonstrations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Trial counts and averaging practices in Appendix A.3 remain identical, including 50 evaluations per LIBERO task and 20 real-world trials per task. No uncertainty estimates, seed information or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes CoT-VLA's average LIBERO score from 81.1% to 83.9%, while its four suite scores remain 87.5, 91.6, 87.6 and 69.0. The revised average matches their rounded mean. All other results and the method ranking are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and embedding, routing and expert-mixture equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about unified planning and execution, scalable atomic skills, long-horizon performance and continual learning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of skill interference, error recovery and CALVIN failure cases are unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the limitations concerning planning accuracy and dependence on human demonstrations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains identical architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing instructions and annotation prompts. The project-page link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and all 68 cited works remain unchanged, including the CoT-VLA reference associated with the corrected table entry.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 8 March 2026 to v2 dated 6 September 2026. Prose, author information, headings and section organization otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes font and placement. Figures, table structures, captions and body layout are otherwise identical; Table 1's substantive edit is numerical only.

improvement.justification: Table 1 corrects CoT-VLA's understated average from 81.1% to 83.9%, consistent with the unchanged suite scores' mean of 83.925%. This provides a limited improvement in numerical accuracy and baseline comparison. The method, remaining evidence, rankings and conclusions are unchanged.
